title: Slow Cooker Smothered Chicken Leg Quarters
cook: 5–6 hr on low, plus 15 min for the gravy

items: 4 chicken leg quarters (about 3 lb total), fully thawed
2 large yellow onions, halved and sliced ½ inch thick
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
4 cups mashed potatoes or steamed rice

steps: Pat the chicken dry. Mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt, black pepper and cayenne, and rub it over every side of the chicken.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the chicken skin side down, in 2 batches if needed, 6–8 min, until deep golden. You're browning it, not cooking it through.
Pour off all but 1 Tbsp of fat. Add the broth and scrape up the browned bits as it bubbles, about 1 min.
Spread the onions, mushrooms and garlic in the slow cooker and add the Worcestershire sauce and bay leaf. Set the chicken on top skin side up and pour the broth from the skillet over it.
Cover and cook on low 5–6 hr, until the meat is tender and the thickest thigh reads at least 175°F.

Move the chicken to a platter and cover with foil. Strain the liquid into a fat separator or measuring cup and skim off the fat. Keep the onions and mushrooms and discard the bay leaf. You need 2 cups of liquid; add more broth if you're short.

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 3–4 min, whisking, until it turns the color of peanut butter. Slowly whisk in the 2 cups of liquid and simmer 3–5 min, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir the onions and mushrooms into the gravy and season with salt to taste. Pour it over the chicken, top with parsley, and serve over mashed potatoes or rice.
tips: Don't skip the sear. It renders fat out of the skin, so the gravy isn't greasy.
The skin goes soft under the gravy, which is how smothered chicken is served. Pull it off before serving if you'd rather.
Add the liquid to the roux a little at a time at first so the gravy stays smooth.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days in the gravy. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat covered in a 350°F oven about 20 min, until it reaches 165°F, adding a splash of broth if the gravy is thick.
